September 29, 2026



The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street, N.E.
Washington, D.C. 20426

Re:      Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., Docket No. ER26-3458-001
         Ameren Services Company, as designated agent for Ameren Illinois Company
         Submission of Substitute First Amended and Restated Distribution Wholesale Umbrella
         Construction Agreement

Dear Secretary Reese:

        On August 7, 2026, Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., ("MISO")1 and Ameren
Services Company ("Ameren Services"), on behalf of Ameren Illinois Company d/b/a Ameren Illinois
("Ameren Illinois," and with Ameren Services, "Ameren") submitted for filing the First Amended and
Restated Distribution Wholesale Umbrella Construction Agreement ("Umbrella Construction
Agreement") between Ameren Illinois and Rural Electric Convenience Cooperative (collectively with
Ameren, the "Parties") in the instant docket (August 7 Filing). It has come to Ameren's attention that the
Umbrella Construction Agreement submitted in the August 7 Filing included confidential and critical
energy infrastructure designations in the template of the appendices to the agreement. The designation
in the appendices without confidential information creates confusion regarding what information is
public or confidential. Therefore, an amended version of the Umbrella Construction Agreement is being
provided to eliminate any confusion about designation of critical energy infrastructure. MISO, on behalf
of the Parties, hereby files an amended version of the Umbrella Construction Agreement ("Substitute
First Revised") to include revised templates in the appendices that eliminate the confidential designation.
The Umbrella Construction Agreement is designated under the MISO Tariff as Service Agreement No.
3064.2



1        As administrator of the MISO Tariff, MISO joins Ameren in this filing under the MISO Tariff but takes no
position on the substance of the filing and reserves the right to comment or protest.
2        MISO notes that it has served a copy of this filing electronically, including attachments, upon all Tariff Customers
under the Tariff, MISO Members, Member representatives of Transmission Owners and Non-Transmission Owners, as well
as all state commissions within the Region. The filing has been posted electronically on MISO’s website at
https://www.misoenergy.org/legal/ferc-filings/ for other interested parties in this matter. In addition, MISO has served a
copy of this filing electronically on all parties to this agreement.
                                                                                                    Page 2 of 2



       The documents submitted with this filing include this transmittal letter and the following;

                       Tab A: Substitute First Revised Distribution Wholesale Umbrella Construction
                       Agreement;

                       Tab B: Redline Substitute First Revised Distribution Wholesale Umbrella
                       Construction Agreement to First Revised Distribution Wholesale Umbrella
                       Agreement; and

                       Tab C: Redline Substitute First Revised Distribution Wholesale Umbrella
                       Construction Agreement to Original Distribution Wholesale Umbrella
                       Agreement.

        For the reasons stated herein and, in the August 7 Filing, Ameren respectfully requests that the
Commission accept the Substitute Original First Amended and Restated Distribution Wholesale
Umbrella Construction Agreement, to be effective October 7, 2026. Additionally, Ameren respectfully
requests that the Commission accept the Substitute Original First Amended and Restated Distribution
Wholesale Umbrella Construction Agreement without modification or condition and grant the requested
effective date of October 7, 2026, sixty-one days after the original filing. Please do not hesitate to contact
the undersigned with any questions.


Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Jennifer S. Moore
Jennifer S. Moore
Senior Corporate Counsel
Ameren Services Company
1901 Chouteau Avenue
St. Louis, MO 63103
jmoore499a@ameren.com
Phone: 314-564-7231

Attorney for Ameren Illinois

                                   First Amended and Restated

                  Distribution Wholesale Umbrella Construction Agreement

         This First Amended and Restated Distribution Wholesale Umbrella Construction
Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into as of June 26, 2026, by and between Rural Electric
Convenience Cooperative, a not-for-profit corporation organized and existing under the laws of
the State of Illinois (“RECC” or “Customer”), and Ameren Illinois Company d/b/a Ameren
Illinois, a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Illinois (“Ameren
Illinois” or “Company”). Customer and Ameren Illinois may be referred to herein individually as
a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.”

                                             RECITALS

         WHEREAS, Customer and Ameren entered into a Distribution Wholesale Umbrella
Construction Agreement dated as of November 13, 2017 (“Original UCA”), to establish the
requirement, terms, and conditions for the connections of Customer's facilities to the Ameren
Illinois Distribution identifying the continuing responsibilities and obligations of the Parties with
respect thereto; and

        WHEREAS, Ameren Illinois owns electric facilities and is engaged in transmission and
distribution of electric power and energy; and

       WHEREAS, Customer owns electric facilities and is engaged in the wholesale sale and
transmission of electric energy to its member cooperatives; and

        WHEREAS, Customer’s electric facilities are connected to the Ameren Illinois
Distribution System and Customer takes Wholesale Distribution Service (“WDS”) from Ameren
Illinois under a Wholesale Distribution Service Agreement (“WDS Agreement”) on file with
FERC; and

        WHEREAS, Customer may, from time to time, request new or additional WDS from
Ameren Illinois that necessitates the construction of certain Modifications to the Ameren Illinois
Distribution System and the Parties desire to establish the terms and conditions for the construction
of, and financial obligations associated with, such Modifications; and

        WHEREAS, Customer and Company had simultaneously entered into the Original UCA
to establish the requirements, terms, and conditions for the connections of Customer’s facilities to
the Ameren Illinois Distribution System, and to define the continuing responsibilities and
obligations of the Parties with respect thereto.

       NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual representations, covenants, and
agreements hereinafter set forth, and intending to be legally bound hereby, the Parties agree as
follows:

1.     PURPOSE AND SCOPE




                                                 1
      1.1      Purpose. The purpose of this Agreement is to set forth the terms and conditions for
              the construction and the financial obligations associated with Modifications to the
              Ameren Illinois Distribution System required in connection with Customer’s request(s)
              for new or additional WDS. The specifications for an individual Modifications project
              shall be set forth in an Attachment A, “Project Specifications,” with financial
              arrangements and geographic and Delivery Point information included in additional
              Attachments A-1 through A-4, as applicable and each such Attachment A package shall
              be filed at FERC in accordance with the Confidential Information provisions in Section
              11.11.

     1.2      Transmission Arrangements. Transmission Service does not fall within the scope of
              this Agreement. All arrangements for Transmission Service must be made under the
              MISO Tariff.

     1.3      Wholesale Distribution Service. The provision of WDS shall be governed by
              Schedule 11 of the MISO Tariff and the WDS Agreement in effect between the Parties,
              as it may be amended to reflect projects governed by this Agreement.

2.         DEFINITIONS

           As used in this Agreement, the capitalized terms shall have the following meanings.

     2.1      “Customer” has the meaning given to it in the preamble of this Agreement.

     2.2      “Customer-Built Facilities” shall mean those facilities associated with Modifications
              to be constructed and owned by Customer, on Customer’s side of the interconnection
              between Company’s Distribution System and Customer’s distribution system.

     2.3      “Delivery Point(s)” shall mean the point or points at which the ownership of the
              Ameren Illinois Distribution System ends and the ownership of the Customer’s system
              begins, and at which point or points Company delivers power to Customer.

     2.4      “Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities” has the meaning given to it in
              Section 4.1 of this Agreement.

     2.5      “Distribution Connection Facilities” has the meaning given to it in Section 4.2 of this
              Agreement.

     2.6      “Distribution System” shall mean the electrical system owned and operated by
              Ameren Illinois to deliver power to customers, which facilities are sized and configured
              at voltage levels appropriately classified and recorded in the plant records of Ameren
              Illinois as distribution plant (generally 12 kV, 34.5 kV, 69 kV or radial 138 kV) and
              used in the provision of Wholesale Distribution Service.

     2.7      “FERC” shall mean the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission or its successor.

     2.8      “Force Majeure” shall mean any act of God, labor disturbance, act of the public
              enemy, war, insurrection, riot, fire, storm or flood, explosion, breakage or accident to


                                                   2
        machinery or equipment, any order, regulation or restriction imposed by governmental,
       military or lawfully established civilian authorities, or any other cause beyond a Party’s
       reasonable control. A Force Majeure event does not include an act of negligence or
       intentional wrongdoing by the Party claiming Force Majeure.

2.9    “Good Utility Practice” shall mean any of the practices, methods and acts engaged in
       or approved by a significant portion of the electric industry during the relevant time
       period, or any of the practices, methods and acts which, in the exercise of reasonable
       judgment in light of the facts known to the time the decision was made, could have
       been expected to accomplish the desired result at a reasonable cost consistent with good
       business practices, reliability, safety and expedition. Good Utility Practice is not
       intended to be limited to the optimum practice, method, or act to the exclusion of all
       others, but rather to be acceptable practices, methods, or acts generally accepted in the
       region, including those practices required by the Federal Power Act Section 215(a)(4).

2.10   “Investment Grade Credit Rating” shall mean with respect to any entity an
       unsecured credit rating (or, if unavailable, an issuer rating or equivalent credit rating)
       of “Baa3” or better from Moody’s and “BBB-” or better from S&P. In case of only a
       single rating being available, that rating will be used to satisfy the condition in the
       preceding sentence.

2.11   “Members” shall mean any entity that is, joins, or becomes a member of Customer
       that has load, electric distribution, or generation within the Ameren Illinois Local
       Balancing Authority, as defined in the MISO Tariff.

2.12   “MISO” shall mean the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., or any
       successor entity(ies) that is responsible for functional control of the operation of part
       or all of the Ameren Illinois transmission facilities.

2.13   “MISO Tariff” shall mean MISO’s Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating
       Reserve Markets Tariff, as it is in effect and may be amended from time to time.

2.14   “Modifications” shall mean the facilities to be constructed, as additions, replacements
       and/or modifications to the Ameren Illinois Distribution System, in connection with
       Customer’s request for new or additional WDS and as described in one or more Project
       Specifications.

2.15   “NERC” shall mean the North American Electric Reliability Corporation or its
       successor.

2.16   “Reasonable Efforts” shall mean, with respect to an action required to be attempted
       or taken by a Party under this Agreement, efforts that are timely and consistent with
       Good Utility Practice and are otherwise substantially equivalent to those a Party would
       use to protect its own interests.

2.17   “Regulatory Requirements” shall mean any FERC policies including NERC
       reliability standards or any applicable regional reliability standards or requirements, or
       policies of MISO or any Governmental/Regulatory Authority having jurisdiction over


                                             3
              the Parties with regard to the subject matter of this Agreement, or any successor to any
             of these.

     2.18    “Transmission Service” has the meaning given to the term in the MISO Tariff.

3.         CONSTRUCTION SECURITY

     3.1     Modifications. The Company shall determine Modifications that will be described in
             the Project Specifications. The Company shall exercise Reasonable Efforts to design,
             engineer, construct, install and place in service (the “Design and Construction
             Process”) the Modifications in accordance with a schedule outlined in the Project
             Specifications. The Company shall begin the Design and Construction Process for the
             Modifications upon execution of the relevant Attachment A, and notes that in the
             normal course construction typically takes approximately 24 months from such date;
             the Company shall exercise commercially reasonable efforts to meet Customer’s
             requested in-service date.

     3.2     Security. The Company may request that Customer provide security for the estimated
             costs of the Modifications, as specified in the Project Specifications, in the form of a
             letter of credit in favor of Ameren Illinois in the amount designated in, and in
             accordance with the specifications of, Attachment A-1 (the “Letter of Credit”) or in
             another form of security acceptable to the Company. Notwithstanding the foregoing,
             Customer shall not be obligated to provide Company with security as long as Customer
             has an Investment Grade Credit Rating.

     3.3     Monitoring and Inspection. Upon reasonable notice, the Company may inspect any
             or all of the Customer-Built Facilities being installed and/or constructed to ensure
             conformity with this Agreement.

4.         COST RESPONSIBILITY

     4.1     Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities. For Modifications required to
             accommodate a request from Customer for the sole benefit of a Delivery Point
             (“Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities”), Customer will compensate the
             Company by means of an up front, lump sum payment, adjusted for income tax gross-
             up. Facilities to which this provision shall apply are tap-related costs, such as
             disconnect switches located in the main line on either side of the Delivery Point, owned
             by Ameren Illinois (“Main Line Switches”), meter structures and other Customer
             driven tap-point modification costs. When a lump sum payment arrangement is
             applied, the lump sum payment shall be equal to the estimated total installed costs to
             be incurred by the Company, plus income tax gross-up at the rate applicable at the time
             the relevant Attachment A is executed, with the income tax gross up amount trued up
             to reflect the rate applicable at the time the Modifications are placed in service.
             Modifications for which a lump sum payment is made under this Section 4.1 shall not
             be included in plant in any future WDS cost of service study or rate. In addition,
             ongoing costs for Good Utility Practice maintenance of such Dedicated Tap-Related
             Connection Facilities shall be billed to Customer as incurred by the Company. Upon



                                                  4
       agreement of the Parties on facilities that require replacement at a later date, Customer
      shall be responsible to the Company for any applicable replacement costs; provided,
      however, that Customer shall not be responsible for any replacement costs caused by
      Company’s gross negligence.

4.2   Distribution Connection Facilities. “Distribution Connection Facilities” are the
      Modifications made to the Distribution System and/or other facilities required to
      connect a Delivery Point to the Distribution System to accommodate the electrical
      service requirements of Customer, which are not Dedicated Tap-Related Connection
      Facilities covered under Section 4.1 of this Agreement or that are not paid for by
      Customer through a System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee as provided in
      Section 4.3 of this Agreement, and which can be found as Attachment A-2 to this
      Agreement. Until such time as the charges for Distribution Connection Facilities are
      included in the monthly charge for WDS as specified in the definition of the Fixed
      Charge below, Customer shall compensate the Company for Distribution Connection
      Facilities on a monthly basis pursuant to the following formula:

                               FC= (DCF x LRS) x FCR
                                        12

      Where:

      FC = Fixed Charge per month applicable to Customer for Distribution Connection
         Facilities. Such Fixed Charge shall be shown on Customer’s monthly invoice from
         Company as a separate line item and shall remain in effect from the first day of the
         month following the Distribution Connection Facilities’ in-service date, to the date
         on which such Distribution Connection Facilities are included in the computation
         of a revised WDS rate placed into effect after the Company's updated cost of service
         study is accepted by the FERC (“Company’s Next WDS Rate Case”), at which time
         any such pre-existing Fixed Charge(s) per month for such Distribution Connection
         Facilities will cease.

      DCF = Cost of the Distribution Connection Facilities. The installed costs (equipment,
        labor and overhead costs) of the Distribution Connection Facilities shall be
        estimated and specified in Section 1.0 of Attachment A, Project Specifications, and
        shall be made up of the costs of lines, poles, substations, switches (includes only
        Company-owned system switches, e.g., switches at three-way corners and bulk
        supply substations, and not Customer-specific or Company-distribution-substation-
        related switches), and all other components of the Distribution System. For
        purposes of this Agreement and without prejudice to the methodology for
        Company’s Next WDS Rate Case, the installed costs of Distribution Connection
        Facilities to be charged through the Fixed Charge will be based on actual cost
        (equipment, labor and overhead costs) net of any plant retired but shall exclude any
        Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities paid for on a lump sum basis.

      LRS = Load Ratio Share (“LRS”) of the relevant Area Distribution System (“ADS”)
        for Customer shall be based on the test year LRS from the Company’s Most Recent


                                            5
          WDS Rate Case in order to equitably allocate the costs of Distribution Connection
         Facilities between Customer and all other retail and wholesale customer loads
         within the ADS. For Distribution Connection Facilities which connect a Delivery
         Point to the ADS but are not part of an ADS to which Customer is then currently
         connected, a different LRS shall be specifically determined based on the
         Customer’s percentage usage of the facilities, and applied consistently with the
         methodology in the Company’s Most Recent WDS Rate Case.

      FCR = Annual Fixed Carrying Charge Rate, which will be determined on a gross plant
        basis and using an FCR rate of 13.50 percent.

4.3   System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee. When, in connection with a
      request for Modifications by the Customer, Customer load growth, as defined in this
      Section 4.3, requires the Company to modify or expand its Distribution System to
      accommodate large new loads served by the Customer, Customer will be subject to a
      System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee in the form of Attachment A-2
      hereto. Such System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee, which will be filed at
      FERC with the Project Specifications, is designed to protect the Company, its
      customers and other stakeholders from the risk that such expected new large load does
      not materialize or produce adequate incremental WDS revenue to support the
      Company’s investment in new facilities.

      Normal load growth on Customer’s system will not be subject to a System Expansion
      and/or Modification Guarantee. The following criteria will be used to determine
      whether system load growth is in excess of normal load growth and therefore subject
      to a System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee:

      4.3.1   In the case where (i) Customer load is served at multiple Delivery Points from
              a single Ameren Illinois distribution line and source substation and (ii)
              Customer identifies a new large load that is expected to increase the combined
              peak demand for all distribution Delivery Points served from that single
              Ameren Illinois distribution line and source substation by the greater of (a) 1
              megawatt (“MW”) or (b) 5% of the peak demand measured in MW over and
              above Customer’s combined Delivery Point forecasted peak demand measured
              in MW for the year Modifications to serve the increase in load are expected to
              be in service. The combined Delivery Point forecasted peak demand shall be
              for only those Delivery Points served from the single Ameren Illinois
              distribution line and source substation.

      4.3.2   In the case where (i) Customer load is served at a single Delivery Point and (ii)
              Customer identifies a new large load that is expected to increase the peak
              demand for the single Delivery Point by the greater of (a) 1 MW or (b) 5% of
              the peak demand measured in MW over and above Customer’s Delivery Point
              forecasted peak demand measured in MW for the year Modifications to serve
              the increase in load are expected to be in service.




                                            6
       If the Modifications provide capacity in excess of the amount necessary to serve
      Customer’s new large load, Customer will be required to guarantee only the portion of
      the costs of Modifications attributable to serving the Customer’s projected new large
      load.

4.4   Identification of Cost Responsibility. The determination as to which Modifications
      are Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities, Distribution Connection Facilities
      and/or facilities subject to a System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee and
      Customer’s cost responsibility for the Modifications will be set forth in the Project
      Specifications to be mutually agreed upon by the Parties, which agreement shall not be
      unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Customer agrees to satisfy its cost
      responsibility specified in a Project Specification for Modifications through a lump
      sum payment, Fixed Charge, or System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee as
      set forth in Sections 4.1, 4.2, and 4.3, as applicable.

4.5   Metering-Related Charges.

      4.5.1   Metering poles or structures are Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities
              and their costs shall be recovered as provided in Section 4.1.

      4.5.2   Existing Delivery Points.

              4.5.2.1 Customer-Owned Meter Replacement Options.

                     If Modifications at an existing Delivery Point for which Customer owns
                     the metering equipment include or cause upgrades or replacement of
                     such metering equipment, Customer has the following options:

                     4.5.2.1.1   Customer may choose to continue to own the upgraded or
                                 replaced metering equipment and there will be no monthly
                                 charge related to such equipment; or

                     4.5.2.1.2   Company shall install and own all metering equipment and
                                 Customer will be allowed to pay for the metering equipment
                                 up front, in a lump sum. The lump sum payment shall be
                                 equal to the estimated total installed costs of the metering
                                 equipment, plus income tax gross-up at the rate applicable at
                                 the time the relevant Attachment A is executed, with the
                                 estimated cost of the metering equipment trued up to actual
                                 cost and the income tax gross up amount trued up to reflect
                                 the rate applicable at the time the metering equipment is
                                 placed in service. Customer shall pay a monthly metering
                                 charge for operations and maintenance of such equipment,
                                 calculated as the cost of the metering equipment multiplied
                                 by 0.0032, which will be reflected in an applicable
                                 Attachment A of this Agreement between Company and
                                 Customer; or



                                           7
                4.5.2.1.3   Company shall install and own all meter equipment and
                           Customer shall pay the metering charge for the applicable
                           voltage level specified in Exhibit A of the WDS Agreement
                           between Company and Customer.

        4.5.2.2 Company-Owned Meter Replacement Options.

               If Modifications at an existing Delivery Point for which Company owns
               the metering equipment include or cause upgrades or replacement of
               such metering equipment,

               4.5.2.2.1   Company will continue to own the upgraded or replaced
                           metering equipment and Customer will be allowed to pay for
                           the metering equipment up front, in a lump sum. The lump
                           sum payment shall be equal to the estimated total installed
                           costs of the metering equipment, plus income tax gross-up at
                           the rate applicable at the time the relevant Attachment A is
                           executed, with the estimated cost of the metering equipment
                           trued up to actual cost and the income tax gross up amount
                           trued up to reflect the rate applicable at the time the metering
                           equipment is placed in service. Customer shall pay a
                           monthly metering charge for operations and maintenance of
                           such equipment, calculated as the cost of the metering
                           equipment, multiplied by 0.0032, which will be reflected in
                           an applicable Attachment A of this Agreement between
                           Company and Customer; or

               4.5.2.2.2   Company will continue to own the upgraded or replaced
                           metering equipment and Customer shall pay the metering
                           charge for the applicable voltage level specified in Exhibit
                           A of the WDS Agreement between Company and Customer.

4.5.3   New Delivery Points.

        If Modifications establish a new Delivery Point, Customer has the following
        options:

        4.5.3.1 Company shall install and own all metering equipment and Customer
                will be allowed to pay for the metering equipment up front, in a lump
                sum. The lump sum payment shall be equal to the estimated total
                installed costs of the metering equipment, plus income tax gross-up at
                the rate applicable at the time the relevant Attachment A is executed,
                with the estimated cost of the metering equipment trued up to actual cost
                and the income tax gross up amount trued up to reflect the rate
                applicable at the time the metering equipment is placed in service.
                Customer shall pay a monthly metering charge for operations and
                maintenance of such equipment, calculated as the cost of the metering



                                      8
                             equipment, multiplied by 0.0032, which will be reflected in Exhibit A
                            of the WDS Agreement between Company and Customer; or

                    4.5.3.2 Company shall install and own all metering equipment and Customer
                            shall pay the metering charge for the applicable voltage level specified
                            in Exhibit A of the WDS Agreement between Company and Customer.

     4.6     Removal Costs. To the extent removal costs associated with Modifications and with
             existing Delivery Point facilities owned by Ameren Illinois (“Removal Costs”) are not
             recovered under the Customer’s WDS Agreement with Company, Customer’s financial
             obligations under this Agreement shall include responsibility for any such unrecovered
             Removal Costs.

     4.7     Invoicing, True Up and Payment. Unless otherwise agreed by Company and
             Customer in an Attachment A, Company shall prepare and provide to Customer a final
             statement that sets forth the final installed costs related to the Modifications. Company
             shall make commercially reasonable efforts to provide the final installed costs within
             ninety (90) days, but shall provide it no later than six months, after (a) completion of
             the design, procurement, construction, installation and testing of the Modifications, or
             (b) earlier termination as provided under Section 7. The final installed costs of the
             Modifications shall include but are not limited to the cost of the design, engineering,
             surveying, equipment procurement, construction, delivery/transportation, setup fees,
             increases/decreases in cost related to commodity prices, the cost effects of currency
             fluctuations, permits, overtime charges (if requested by Customer), termination costs,
             related applicable taxes, and any other charges or costs reasonably incurred by
             Company in connection with the design, construction and installation of the
             Modifications. The final statement shall reflect true up of the tax gross up amount
             following the in-service date for the Modifications, as provided for in Sections 4.1 and
             4.5, and true up of estimated costs of metering equipment to actual installed costs of
             metering equipment, as provided for in Section 4.5. Customer shall remit to Company
             any amounts shown owing by Customer on the final statement within ten (10) business
             days of receipt of the final statement or within such period as the Parties may mutually
             agree upon. If the up front payment(s) made by Customer, based on cost estimates,
             exceed Company’s actual costs, Company will reimburse Customer for such excess
             payment within 30 days of determining excess payment(s) were made. If requested by
             Customer, Company will provide detailed documentation supporting its actual costs.

5.         FORCE MAJEURE

     5.1     Except for obligations to make any payments under a filed Attachment A Project
             Specifications and to comply with the provisions of this Agreement, the Company and
             Customer shall be excused from performing their respective obligations under any filed
             Attachment A Project Specifications and shall not be liable in damages or otherwise if
             and to the extent that they are unable to so perform or are prevented from performing
             by an event of Force Majeure, provided that:




                                                   9
              5.1.1   the non-performing Party, as promptly as practicable after the Party reasonably
                     determines that a Force Majeure event has occurred and such Force Majeure
                     event will adversely affect the Party’s ability to perform its obligations under
                     Attachment A, gives the other Party written notice describing the particulars of
                     the occurrence, including a reasonable estimation of the event of Force
                     Majeure’s expected duration and the probable impact on the performance of the
                     non-performing Party’s obligations under Attachment A;

             5.1.2   the suspension of performance is of no greater scope and of no longer duration
                     than is reasonably required by the event of Force Majeure;

             5.1.3   the non-performing Party uses all Reasonable Efforts to remedy its inability to
                     perform; and

             5.1.4   as soon as the non-performing Party is able to resume performance of its

                                   First Amended and Restated

                  Distribution Wholesale Umbrella Construction Agreement

         This First Amended and Restated Distribution Wholesale Umbrella Construction
Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into as of June 26, 2026, by and between Rural Electric
Convenience Cooperative, a not-for-profit corporation organized and existing under the laws of
the State of Illinois (“RECC” or “Customer”), and Ameren Illinois Company d/b/a Ameren
Illinois, a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Illinois (“Ameren
Illinois” or “Company”). Customer and Ameren Illinois may be referred to herein individually as
a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.”

                                             RECITALS

         WHEREAS, Customer and Ameren entered into a Distribution Wholesale Umbrella
Construction Agreement dated as of November 13, 2017 (“Original UCA”), to establish the
requirement, terms, and conditions for the connections of Customer's facilities to the Ameren
Illinois Distribution identifying the continuing responsibilities and obligations of the Parties with
respect thereto; and

        WHEREAS, Ameren Illinois owns electric facilities and is engaged in transmission and
distribution of electric power and energy; and

       WHEREAS, Customer owns electric facilities and is engaged in the wholesale sale and
transmission of electric energy to its member cooperatives; and

        WHEREAS, Customer’s electric facilities are connected to the Ameren Illinois
Distribution System and Customer takes Wholesale Distribution Service (“WDS”) from Ameren
Illinois under a Wholesale Distribution Service Agreement (“WDS Agreement”) on file with
FERC; and

        WHEREAS, Customer may, from time to time, request new or additional WDS from
Ameren Illinois that necessitates the construction of certain Modifications to the Ameren Illinois
Distribution System and the Parties desire to establish the terms and conditions for the construction
of, and financial obligations associated with, such Modifications; and

        WHEREAS, Customer and Company had simultaneously entered into the Original UCA
to establish the requirements, terms, and conditions for the connections of Customer’s facilities to
the Ameren Illinois Distribution System, and to define the continuing responsibilities and
obligations of the Parties with respect thereto.

       NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual representations, covenants, and
agreements hereinafter set forth, and intending to be legally bound hereby, the Parties agree as
follows:

1.     PURPOSE AND SCOPE




                                                 1
      1.1      Purpose. The purpose of this Agreement is to set forth the terms and conditions for
              the construction and the financial obligations associated with Modifications to the
              Ameren Illinois Distribution System required in connection with Customer’s request(s)
              for new or additional WDS. The specifications for an individual Modifications project
              shall be set forth in an Attachment A, “Project Specifications,” with financial
              arrangements and geographic and Delivery Point information included in additional
              Attachments A-1 through A-4, as applicable and each such Attachment A package shall
              be filed at FERC in accordance with the Confidential Information provisions in Section
              11.11.

     1.2      Transmission Arrangements. Transmission Service does not fall within the scope of
              this Agreement. All arrangements for Transmission Service must be made under the
              MISO Tariff.

     1.3      Wholesale Distribution Service. The provision of WDS shall be governed by
              Schedule 11 of the MISO Tariff and the WDS Agreement in effect between the Parties,
              as it may be amended to reflect projects governed by this Agreement.

2.         DEFINITIONS

           As used in this Agreement, the capitalized terms shall have the following meanings.

     2.1      “Customer” has the meaning given to it in the preamble of this Agreement.

     2.2      “Customer-Built Facilities” shall mean those facilities associated with Modifications
              to be constructed and owned by Customer, on Customer’s side of the interconnection
              between Company’s Distribution System and Customer’s distribution system.

     2.3      “Delivery Point(s)” shall mean the point or points at which the ownership of the
              Ameren Illinois Distribution System ends and the ownership of the Customer’s system
              begins, and at which point or points Company delivers power to Customer.

     2.4      “Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities” has the meaning given to it in
              Section 4.1 of this Agreement.

     2.5      “Distribution Connection Facilities” has the meaning given to it in Section 4.2 of this
              Agreement.

     2.6      “Distribution System” shall mean the electrical system owned and operated by
              Ameren Illinois to deliver power to customers, which facilities are sized and configured
              at voltage levels appropriately classified and recorded in the plant records of Ameren
              Illinois as distribution plant (generally 12 kV, 34.5 kV, 69 kV or radial 138 kV) and
              used in the provision of Wholesale Distribution Service.

     2.7      “FERC” shall mean the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission or its successor.

     2.8      “Force Majeure” shall mean any act of God, labor disturbance, act of the public
              enemy, war, insurrection, riot, fire, storm or flood, explosion, breakage or accident to


                                                   2
        machinery or equipment, any order, regulation or restriction imposed by governmental,
       military or lawfully established civilian authorities, or any other cause beyond a Party’s
       reasonable control. A Force Majeure event does not include an act of negligence or
       intentional wrongdoing by the Party claiming Force Majeure.

2.9    “Good Utility Practice” shall mean any of the practices, methods and acts engaged in
       or approved by a significant portion of the electric industry during the relevant time
       period, or any of the practices, methods and acts which, in the exercise of reasonable
       judgment in light of the facts known to the time the decision was made, could have
       been expected to accomplish the desired result at a reasonable cost consistent with good
       business practices, reliability, safety and expedition. Good Utility Practice is not
       intended to be limited to the optimum practice, method, or act to the exclusion of all
       others, but rather to be acceptable practices, methods, or acts generally accepted in the
       region, including those practices required by the Federal Power Act Section 215(a)(4).

2.10   “Investment Grade Credit Rating” shall mean with respect to any entity an
       unsecured credit rating (or, if unavailable, an issuer rating or equivalent credit rating)
       of “Baa3” or better from Moody’s and “BBB-” or better from S&P. In case of only a
       single rating being available, that rating will be used to satisfy the condition in the
       preceding sentence.

2.11   “Members” shall mean any entity that is, joins, or becomes a member of Customer
       that has load, electric distribution, or generation within the Ameren Illinois Local
       Balancing Authority, as defined in the MISO Tariff.

2.12   “MISO” shall mean the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., or any
       successor entity(ies) that is responsible for functional control of the operation of part
       or all of the Ameren Illinois transmission facilities.

2.13   “MISO Tariff” shall mean MISO’s Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating
       Reserve Markets Tariff, as it is in effect and may be amended from time to time.

2.14   “Modifications” shall mean the facilities to be constructed, as additions, replacements
       and/or modifications to the Ameren Illinois Distribution System, in connection with
       Customer’s request for new or additional WDS and as described in one or more Project
       Specifications.

2.15   “NERC” shall mean the North American Electric Reliability Corporation or its
       successor.

2.16   “Reasonable Efforts” shall mean, with respect to an action required to be attempted
       or taken by a Party under this Agreement, efforts that are timely and consistent with
       Good Utility Practice and are otherwise substantially equivalent to those a Party would
       use to protect its own interests.

2.17   “Regulatory Requirements” shall mean any FERC policies including NERC
       reliability standards or any applicable regional reliability standards or requirements, or
       policies of MISO or any Governmental/Regulatory Authority having jurisdiction over


                                             3
              the Parties with regard to the subject matter of this Agreement, or any successor to any
             of these.

     2.18    “Transmission Service” has the meaning given to the term in the MISO Tariff.

3.         CONSTRUCTION SECURITY

     3.1     Modifications. The Company shall determine Modifications that will be described in
             the Project Specifications. The Company shall exercise Reasonable Efforts to design,
             engineer, construct, install and place in service (the “Design and Construction
             Process”) the Modifications in accordance with a schedule outlined in the Project
             Specifications. The Company shall begin the Design and Construction Process for the
             Modifications upon execution of the relevant Attachment A, and notes that in the
             normal course construction typically takes approximately 24 months from such date;
             the Company shall exercise commercially reasonable efforts to meet Customer’s
             requested in-service date.

     3.2     Security. The Company may request that Customer provide security for the estimated
             costs of the Modifications, as specified in the Project Specifications, in the form of a
             letter of credit in favor of Ameren Illinois in the amount designated in, and in
             accordance with the specifications of, Attachment A-1 (the “Letter of Credit”) or in
             another form of security acceptable to the Company. Notwithstanding the foregoing,
             Customer shall not be obligated to provide Company with security as long as Customer
             has an Investment Grade Credit Rating.

     3.3     Monitoring and Inspection. Upon reasonable notice, the Company may inspect any
             or all of the Customer-Built Facilities being installed and/or constructed to ensure
             conformity with this Agreement.

4.         COST RESPONSIBILITY

     4.1     Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities. For Modifications required to
             accommodate a request from Customer for the sole benefit of a Delivery Point
             (“Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities”), Customer will compensate the
             Company by means of an up front, lump sum payment, adjusted for income tax gross-
             up. Facilities to which this provision shall apply are tap-related costs, such as
             disconnect switches located in the main line on either side of the Delivery Point, owned
             by Ameren Illinois (“Main Line Switches”), meter structures and other Customer
             driven tap-point modification costs. When a lump sum payment arrangement is
             applied, the lump sum payment shall be equal to the estimated total installed costs to
             be incurred by the Company, plus income tax gross-up at the rate applicable at the time
             the relevant Attachment A is executed, with the income tax gross up amount trued up
             to reflect the rate applicable at the time the Modifications are placed in service.
             Modifications for which a lump sum payment is made under this Section 4.1 shall not
             be included in plant in any future WDS cost of service study or rate. In addition,
             ongoing costs for Good Utility Practice maintenance of such Dedicated Tap-Related
             Connection Facilities shall be billed to Customer as incurred by the Company. Upon



                                                  4
       agreement of the Parties on facilities that require replacement at a later date, Customer
      shall be responsible to the Company for any applicable replacement costs; provided,
      however, that Customer shall not be responsible for any replacement costs caused by
      Company’s gross negligence.

4.2   Distribution Connection Facilities. “Distribution Connection Facilities” are the
      Modifications made to the Distribution System and/or other facilities required to
      connect a Delivery Point to the Distribution System to accommodate the electrical
      service requirements of Customer, which are not Dedicated Tap-Related Connection
      Facilities covered under Section 4.1 of this Agreement or that are not paid for by
      Customer through a System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee as provided in
      Section 4.3 of this Agreement, and which can be found as Attachment A-2 to this
      Agreement. Until such time as the charges for Distribution Connection Facilities are
      included in the monthly charge for WDS as specified in the definition of the Fixed
      Charge below, Customer shall compensate the Company for Distribution Connection
      Facilities on a monthly basis pursuant to the following formula:

                               FC= (DCF x LRS) x FCR
                                        12

      Where:

      FC = Fixed Charge per month applicable to Customer for Distribution Connection
         Facilities. Such Fixed Charge shall be shown on Customer’s monthly invoice from
         Company as a separate line item and shall remain in effect from the first day of the
         month following the Distribution Connection Facilities’ in-service date, to the date
         on which such Distribution Connection Facilities are included in the computation
         of a revised WDS rate placed into effect after the Company's updated cost of service
         study is accepted by the FERC (“Company’s Next WDS Rate Case”), at which time
         any such pre-existing Fixed Charge(s) per month for such Distribution Connection
         Facilities will cease.

      DCF = Cost of the Distribution Connection Facilities. The installed costs (equipment,
        labor and overhead costs) of the Distribution Connection Facilities shall be
        estimated and specified in Section 1.0 of Attachment A, Project Specifications, and
        shall be made up of the costs of lines, poles, substations, switches (includes only
        Company-owned system switches, e.g., switches at three-way corners and bulk
        supply substations, and not Customer-specific or Company-distribution-substation-
        related switches), and all other components of the Distribution System. For
        purposes of this Agreement and without prejudice to the methodology for
        Company’s Next WDS Rate Case, the installed costs of Distribution Connection
        Facilities to be charged through the Fixed Charge will be based on actual cost
        (equipment, labor and overhead costs) net of any plant retired but shall exclude any
        Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities paid for on a lump sum basis.

      LRS = Load Ratio Share (“LRS”) of the relevant Area Distribution System (“ADS”)
        for Customer shall be based on the test year LRS from the Company’s Most Recent


                                            5
          WDS Rate Case in order to equitably allocate the costs of Distribution Connection
         Facilities between Customer and all other retail and wholesale customer loads
         within the ADS. For Distribution Connection Facilities which connect a Delivery
         Point to the ADS but are not part of an ADS to which Customer is then currently
         connected, a different LRS shall be specifically determined based on the
         Customer’s percentage usage of the facilities, and applied consistently with the
         methodology in the Company’s Most Recent WDS Rate Case.

      FCR = Annual Fixed Carrying Charge Rate, which will be determined on a gross plant
        basis and using an FCR rate of 13.50 percent.

4.3   System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee. When, in connection with a
      request for Modifications by the Customer, Customer load growth, as defined in this
      Section 4.3, requires the Company to modify or expand its Distribution System to
      accommodate large new loads served by the Customer, Customer will be subject to a
      System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee in the form of Attachment A-2
      hereto. Such System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee, which will be filed at
      FERC with the Project Specifications, is designed to protect the Company, its
      customers and other stakeholders from the risk that such expected new large load does
      not materialize or produce adequate incremental WDS revenue to support the
      Company’s investment in new facilities.

      Normal load growth on Customer’s system will not be subject to a System Expansion
      and/or Modification Guarantee. The following criteria will be used to determine
      whether system load growth is in excess of normal load growth and therefore subject
      to a System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee:

      4.3.1   In the case where (i) Customer load is served at multiple Delivery Points from
              a single Ameren Illinois distribution line and source substation and (ii)
              Customer identifies a new large load that is expected to increase the combined
              peak demand for all distribution Delivery Points served from that single
              Ameren Illinois distribution line and source substation by the greater of (a) 1
              megawatt (“MW”) or (b) 5% of the peak demand measured in MW over and
              above Customer’s combined Delivery Point forecasted peak demand measured
              in MW for the year Modifications to serve the increase in load are expected to
              be in service. The combined Delivery Point forecasted peak demand shall be
              for only those Delivery Points served from the single Ameren Illinois
              distribution line and source substation.

      4.3.2   In the case where (i) Customer load is served at a single Delivery Point and (ii)
              Customer identifies a new large load that is expected to increase the peak
              demand for the single Delivery Point by the greater of (a) 1 MW or (b) 5% of
              the peak demand measured in MW over and above Customer’s Delivery Point
              forecasted peak demand measured in MW for the year Modifications to serve
              the increase in load are expected to be in service.




                                            6
       If the Modifications provide capacity in excess of the amount necessary to serve
      Customer’s new large load, Customer will be required to guarantee only the portion of
      the costs of Modifications attributable to serving the Customer’s projected new large
      load.

4.4   Identification of Cost Responsibility. The determination as to which Modifications
      are Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities, Distribution Connection Facilities
      and/or facilities subject to a System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee and
      Customer’s cost responsibility for the Modifications will be set forth in the Project
      Specifications to be mutually agreed upon by the Parties, which agreement shall not be
      unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Customer agrees to satisfy its cost
      responsibility specified in a Project Specification for Modifications through a lump
      sum payment, Fixed Charge, or System Expansion and/or Modification Guarantee as
      set forth in Sections 4.1, 4.2, and 4.3, as applicable.

4.5   Metering-Related Charges.

      4.5.1   Metering poles or structures are Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities
              and their costs shall be recovered as provided in Section 4.1.

      4.5.2   Existing Delivery Points.

              4.5.2.1 Customer-Owned Meter Replacement Options.

                     If Modifications at an existing Delivery Point for which Customer owns
                     the metering equipment include or cause upgrades or replacement of
                     such metering equipment, Customer has the following options:

                     4.5.2.1.1   Customer may choose to continue to own the upgraded or
                                 replaced metering equipment and there will be no monthly
                                 charge related to such equipment; or

                     4.5.2.1.2   Company shall install and own all metering equipment and
                                 Customer will be allowed to pay for the metering equipment
                                 up front, in a lump sum. The lump sum payment shall be
                                 equal to the estimated total installed costs of the metering
                                 equipment, plus income tax gross-up at the rate applicable at
                                 the time the relevant Attachment A is executed, with the

individually as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.”

                                             RECITALS

         WHEREAS, Customer and Ameren entered into a Distribution Wholesale Umbrella
Construction Agreement dated as of November 13, 2017 (“Original UCA”), to establish the
requirement, terms, and conditions for the connections of Customer's facilities to the Ameren
Illinois Distribution identifying the continuing responsibilities and obligations of the Parties with
respect thereto; and

        WHEREAS, Ameren Illinois owns electric facilities and is engaged in transmission and
distribution of electric power and energy; and

       WHEREAS, Customer owns electric facilities and is engaged in the wholesale sale and
transmission of electric energy to its member cooperatives; and

         WHEREAS, Customer’s electric facilities are connected to the Ameren Illinois
Distribution System and Customer takes Wholesale Distribution Service (“WDS”) from Ameren
Illinois under a Wholesale Distribution Service Agreement (“WDS Agreement”) to be filedon file
with FERC; and

        WHEREAS, Customer may, from time to time, request new or additional WDS from
Ameren Illinois that necessitates the construction of certain Modifications to the Ameren Illinois
Distribution System and the Parties desire to establish the terms and conditions for the construction
of, and financial obligations associated with, such Modifications; and

        WHEREAS, Customer and Company arehad simultaneously enteringentered into a
Wholesale Connection Agreementthe Original UCA to establish the requirements, terms, and
conditions for the connections of Customer’s facilities to the Ameren Illinois Distribution System,
and to define the continuing responsibilities and obligations of the Parties with respect thereto.

       NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual representations, covenants, and
agreements hereinafter set forth, and intending to be legally bound hereby, the Parties agree as
follows:

1.     PURPOSE AND SCOPE




                                                 1

     1.1      Purpose. The purpose of this Agreement is to set forth the terms and conditions for
              the construction and the financial obligations associated with Modifications to the
              Ameren Illinois Distribution System required in connection with Customer’s request(s)
              for new or additional WDS. The specifications for an individual Modifications project
              shall be set forth in an Attachment A, “Project Specifications,” with financial
              arrangements and geographic and Delivery Point information included in additional
              Attachments A-1 through A-4, as applicable and each such Attachment A package shall
              be filed at FERC in accordance with the Confidential Information provisions in Section
              11.11.

     1.2      Transmission Arrangements. Transmission Service does not fall within the scope of
              this Agreement. All arrangements for Transmission Service must be made under the
              MISO Tariff.

     1.3      Wholesale Distribution Service. The provision of WDS shall be governed by
              Schedule 11 of the MISO Tariff and the WDS Agreement in effect between the Parties,
              as it may be amended to reflect projects governed by this Agreement.

2.         DEFINITIONS

           As used in this Agreement, the capitalized terms shall have the following meanings.

     2.1      “Customer” has the meaning given to it in the preamble of this Agreement.

     2.2      “Customer-Built Facilities” shall mean those facilities associated with Modifications
              to be constructed and owned by Customer, on Customer’s side of the interconnection
              between Company’s Distribution System and Customer’s distribution system.

     2.3      “Delivery Point(s)” shall mean the point or points at which the ownership of the
              Ameren Illinois Distribution System ends and the ownership of the Customer’s system
              begins, and at which point or points Company delivers power to Customer.

     2.4      “Dedicated Tap-Related Connection Facilities” has the meaning given to it in
              Section 4.1 of this Agreement.

     2.5      “Distribution Connection Facilities” has the meaning given to it in Section 4.2 of this
              Agreement.

     2.6      “Distribution System” shall mean the electrical system owned and operated by
              Ameren Illinois to deliver power to customers, which facilities are sized and configured
              at voltage levels appropriately classified and recorded in the plant records of Ameren
              Illinois as distribution plant (generally 12 kV, 34.5 kV, 69 kV or radial 138 kV) and
              used in the provision of Wholesale Distribution Service.

     2.7      “FERC” shall mean the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission or its successor.

     2.8      “Force Majeure” shall mean any act of God, labor disturbance, act of the public
              enemy, war, insurrection, riot, fire, storm or flood, explosion, breakage or accident to


                                                   2
                                                                          EXECUTION COPY


       machinery or equipment, any order, regulation or restriction imposed by governmental,
       military or lawfully established civilian authorities, or any other cause beyond a Party’s
       reasonable control. A Force Majeure event does not include an act of negligence or
       intentional wrongdoing by the Party claiming Force Majeure.

2.9    “Good Utility Practice” shall mean any of the practices, methods and acts engaged in
       or approved by a significant portion of the electric industry during the relevant time
       period, or any of the practices, methods and acts which, in the exercise of reasonable
       judgment in light of the facts known to the time the decision was made, could have
       been expected to accomplish the desired result at a reasonable cost consistent with good
       business practices, reliability, safety and expedition. Good Utility Practice is not
       intended to be limited to the optimum practice, method, or act to the exclusion of all
       others, but rather to be acceptable practices, methods, or acts generally accepted in the
       region, including those practices required by the Federal Power Act Section 215(a)(4).

2.10   “Investment Grade Credit Rating” shall mean with respect to any entity an
       unsecured credit rating (or, if unavailable, an issuer rating or equivalent credit rating)

2.13   “MISO Tariff” shall mean MISO’s Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating

3.         CONSTRUCTION SECURITY

     3.1     Modifications. The Company shall determine Modifications that will be described in
